title: assure record writes the same predicate for the same run, for the attestation action to sign with the commit as subject
steps: With a fixture repository whose spec has three automated test records, go test -json output and Python runner output: assure record runs at the commit checked out, as a job of the trusted workflow.
assure record writes the proof run predicate under the runner's temporary folder, and the attest job's subject step of proof-run.yml names the commit as the subject.
assure record runs again with the same inputs and another predicate file.
On the refused path: assure record runs on go test -json output in which a test names an ID that is not a test record.
expected_result: It exits 0 and reports 3 outcomes, 2 passed and 1 failed. The predicate is exactly the expected document: the commit, the provider, the run reference, the first and the last event time, the spec digest, and the outcomes in ID order, with did not run for the test that did not run. The subject step names the commit as the subject, with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest. The second run writes the same bytes. The refused run exits non-zero, names the unknown ID and writes no predicate.

title: assure gate change measures both commits, verifies the proof run at the change, compares the code faults of both, and prints the decision with every cause
steps: With a fixture repository whose spec differs between the base head and the change, which adds an obligation, and a passed proof run signed at the change's own ref: assure gate change runs as the gate job of a pull request, with a signature check that stands for the provider's at the adapter's edge.

assure gate change measures the coverage at both commits with the real Lathe CLI, verifies the proof run, reads the code faults of both trees and reports the base head's fault as present at base, and prints the decision and writes it to the step summary.
On the refused path: assure gate change runs for a change under which a share fell and a proof failed.
On the refused path: assure gate change runs for a change that alters a workflow file, with a proof run signed at its own ref.
On the refused path: assure gate change runs for a change that adds a Go file no record names.
expected_result: The main run exits 0 with exactly the expected decision: both commits, both coverages, the proof run with its signer and log entry, the code fault of the base head reported as present at base, and no reason; the step summary holds the same text. The first refused run exits non-zero and names each obligation that fell from built and the failed test. The second refused run exits non-zero, takes no proof run, and names the workflow file. The third refused run exits non-zero and names the new file with its rule and key as its one reason, and still reports the base head's fault as present at base.

title: assure gate release passes a fully proved commit and writes the decision predicate, and refuses every other commit with each cause named
steps: With a fixture repository whose release commit has every obligation designed, built and proved and no code-standard fault, and a passed proof run signed at main: assure gate release runs as the gate-release job of a push to main, with a signature check that stands for the provider's at the adapter's edge.

assure gate release measures the coverage with the real Lathe CLI, verifies the proof run, reads the commit's tree against the code standard, prints the decision, writes it to the step summary, and writes the decision predicate under the runner's temporary folder; the attest-release job's subject step names the commit as the subject.
assure gate release runs again with the same inputs and another predicate file.

On the refused paths: assure gate release runs at a commit with an obligation not proved, with a proof run in which a test failed, with a proof run signed at a pull request's ref, and at a commit whose tree has a Go file no record names.
expected_result: The main run exits 0 with exactly the expected decision: the commit, its coverage of 100% for each share, the proof run with its signer and log entry, the attestation the trusted signer at main is to make, no code fault and no reason, then the predicate's path and digest; the step summary holds the same decision. The predicate is exactly the expected document: the commit, the kind release, the coverage, passed, no reason, no code fault, and the proof run's identity. The subject step names the commit, with the SHA-256 of its ID as the digest. The second run writes the same bytes. Each refused run exits 1, writes no predicate, ends with one notice line that gives the number of reasons, and names its cause: the obligation not proved, the failed test, the ref the proof run is signed at, and the file with its rule.

title: assure ledger fetches and verifies the proof runs of a commit and its history, prints each test record with its result and where it last passed, and shows a refused attestation as none with why
steps: With a fixture repository of five commits and attestations stubbed at the adapter's edge: assure ledger runs for the newest commit, whose proof run has one test failed, with no attestation at the commit before it, a forged one before that, and a passed one before that.
assure ledger runs again with the attestation at the newest commit forged.
expected_result: The first run prints the whole ledger: each test record with its state, result and the commit it last passed at, the release-grade proof run, the refused ancestor with the verifier's reason and the test records that did not pass; it asks the store for four commits, each once, and exits 1. The second run shows no result at the commit, says that none is verified there at release grade, gives the verifier's reason, and exits 1.

title: An author scaffolds an rpc-service declaration that checking accepts as written
steps: In an empty project folder with the configuration of ST-DECL-TD01: stego init --archetype rpc-service runs.
The test reads the files that stego init wrote and printed.
stego validate runs with no change to any file.
expected_result: Expects stego init to exit 0 and to print the project name and each file it created: the declaration, the minimal proto file of the archetype and the fills folder, with the configuration kept as it was. Expects stego validate to exit 0 with no fault.
notes: Not automated yet: the test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in an empty temporary project folder.

title: An agent reads, as structured data, every component, setting and slot it may declare for rest-crud
steps: With the registry of ST-DECL-TD01: the report runs for rest-crud as structured data.
The test parses the output and compares it with the components, settings, allowed values and slots that the fixture registry's files state for rest-crud.
expected_result: Expects exit 0, one JSON document, and the same components, settings with their types and allowed values, and slots as the fixture registry states, with none missing and none more.
notes: Not automated yet: the report (ST-SUP-QRY01) is not built. stego registry inspect (ST-SUP-CLI02) presents the query today, for one component and as text, with no archetype input and no structured output. The test runs the stego command that presents the query for an archetype, as structured data, once the CLI names it. The test reads the expected components, settings and slots from the fixture registry's own files, not from the code under test.

title: An author checks a declaration, sees every fault, and the project is unchanged
steps: The test records the bytes of every file in the project of ST-DECL-TD02.
stego validate runs on TD02 unchanged.
The test changes TD02 to hold three faults: a second entity named Todo, a binding with the operator merge, and a field type strng. stego validate runs again.
The test compares every file in the project with the recorded bytes, with the three changes left out.
expected_result: Expects the first run to exit 0 with no fault, and the second to exit non-zero with the three faults. Expects no file to be made, changed or removed by either run.
notes: Not automated yet: the structured faults are not built. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test.

title: An agent repairs a refused declaration from the structured faults alone
steps: ST-DECL-TD02 is changed to hold three faults: a second entity named Todo, a binding on todos at before_create with the operator merge, and the type strng on the field done. stego validate runs with its structured output.
A scripted agent changes the declaration only at the path of each fault, to a value the fault allows or to a new name, and runs stego validate again.
The scripted agent compares the new faults with the old ones, repairs those that remain, and runs stego validate again, until it accepts the declaration.
expected_result: Expects stego validate to accept the declaration by the third run, with the scripted agent reading nothing but the structured faults.
notes: Not automated yet: stego validate has no structured output yet (ST-DECL-CLI02). The test asks for it in the form that ST-DECL-CLI02 names once it is built.

title: An author declares tenancy, audit, tenant kinds and sensitivity, and checking accepts them with the defaults filled in
steps: ST-DECL-TD02 is changed to say tenancy kind pooled with the key org_id and the claim org.id, to give no audit setting, to add a shared entity Plan and a system entity Job with no collection, and to mark the field title pii.
stego validate runs.
expected_result: Expects exit 0 and the settings that checking reports to hold the claim path org.id, tenancy pooled, audit at level change with a SHA-256 chain and an anchor, Todo owned, Plan shared, Job system, and title pii.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in a temporary project folder. stego validate does not yet give back the settings it filled in (ST-DECL-CLI02); flow step ST-DECL-UC05-FL-S02 says checking reports them, and the test reads them from that report.

title: An author binds authorization to a schema in the service source, and checking compiles it and accepts the declaration
steps: ST-DECL-TD02 is changed to name the provider spicedb, the schema path authz/schema.zed with the fixture schema of ST-DECL-TD03, the subject from identity user, and the resource type, permissions and relationship of Todo.
A binding on todos at after_create lists document#viewer in Relationships written.
stego validate runs.
expected_result: Expects exit 0 and no fault, which needs checking to compile the schema and to find every name it uses.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in a temporary project folder. Checking compiles the fixture schema with the schema compiler of the provider's port.

title: An author declares idempotency, and checking accepts it with create among the required operations
steps: ST-DECL-TD02 is changed to add patch to todos and to declare idempotency required on create and patch, with the retention 48h and the fingerprint body.
stego validate runs.
expected_result: Expects exit 0 and the settings that checking reports to hold Required on create and patch, the retention 48h and the fingerprint over the method, the path and the body.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in a temporary project folder.

title: An author declares a ledger with its accounts and a transfers collection, and checking accepts it
steps: ST-DECL-TD02 is changed to add the entity Wallet of kind ledger with the currency EUR, the transfer codes topup, purchase and refund, two phase yes, the pending timeout 15m and snapshot every 3, and the accounts customer_wallet and settlement as in ST-DECL-TD04.
A collection transfers over Wallet allows create, post, void, reverse, read and list.
stego validate runs.
expected_result: Expects exit 0 and no fault.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in a temporary project folder. The transfer rule of ST-DECL-UC08-R06 waits on ST-DECL-Q02.

title: An author declares modes, mixins, a controller and declared invariants, and checking accepts them
steps: ST-DECL-TD02 is changed to declare no modes and the mixin durable-events.
It adds a controller provisioner with sources scan and watch, resync 10m, replicas 2, lease TTL 15s and tenants each, and a declared invariant unique on Todo by title.
stego validate runs.
expected_result: Expects exit 0, no fault, and the modes api, worker and controller in the settings that checking reports.
notes: Not automated yet: checking does not hold this rule yet. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test in a temporary project folder.

title: The platform engineer names every service built from a digest and gets the fleet's VEX statements
steps: From ST-DIS-TD02: the platform engineer runs stego fleet --digest D1 on the six checkouts.
The platform engineer runs stego fleet vex on the checkouts alpha, bravo, charlie and delta.
expected_result: The first run names alpha and bravo with A 1.2.0 and D1, and names echo and foxtrot as unknown. The second run prints eight OpenVEX statements with the statuses of ST-DIS-UC02-R04-T01. Neither run uses the network or writes a file.
notes: It runs the binary in a network namespace with no interface but loopback (unshare -n, as an unprivileged user), so that any network call fails.

title: A component fix reaches a consumer by a supersession and a registry pin bump, with no compiler release
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03: the platform engineer changes component A, and the registry at R2 holds its new digest DA2.
The platform engineer runs stego lifecycle supersede for DA1 with the successor DA2, a fail date of T+90 days, and no declaration or fill change needed.
The consumer moves the registry pin to R2, keeps its compiler, and runs stego apply.
On the refused path: stego lifecycle supersede runs with no successor.
expected_result: The supersession is recorded. The consumer's apply exits 0, changes only component A's files and the record, and the record keeps the compiler build. The refused run exits non-zero, names the successor, and records nothing.
notes: The flags of stego lifecycle supersede and stego lifecycle withdraw are not decided yet (ST-DIS-CLI01, ST-DIS-CLI02); the builder names them. The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A service author learns of a superseded pin while working, and past its date the pin fails
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03 with the standing variant of ST-DIS-TD01: the service author runs stego validate and stego plan.
The variant changes to past, and the author runs stego validate.
The author runs stego apply.
On the unchecked path: the lifecycle records cannot be read, and the author runs stego validate.
expected_result: The first two runs exit 0 and report DA1 superseded by DA2 with its fail date. Past the date validate exits non-zero for DA1, and apply exits non-zero and writes nothing. On the unchecked path validate says that it could not check and reports no pin as current.
notes: The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A withdrawal names its consumers first, and after its date every pinning service fails validate
steps: From ST-DIS-TD02 with ADV-3 removed: the platform engineer runs stego fleet --digest E1 on the six checkouts.
The platform engineer runs stego lifecycle withdraw for E1 with a reason and a fail date of T+30 days.
The date passes, and stego validate runs in bravo and in charlie.
On the refused path: stego lifecycle withdraw runs for E1 with a date of T-1 days.
expected_result: The sweep names bravo and charlie. The withdrawal is recorded. After the date validate exits non-zero in both and names E1. The refused run exits non-zero and records nothing.
notes: The validate step needs checkouts that stego validate can read, with their declarations and the registry. The flags of stego lifecycle supersede and stego lifecycle withdraw are not decided yet (ST-DIS-CLI01, ST-DIS-CLI02); the builder names them. The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam.

title: A release is qualified at exactly its commit, verified as a consumer installs it, and each refused path fails
steps: A commit with a passed release decision attested by proof-run.yml at main, a successful checks run, and a successful signed artifact run: qualify-compiler-release.py runs with --revision for that commit.
The script fetches and verifies the release decision at that commit.
The script finds the checks run and the signed artifact run at that commit and reads the conclusion of every required job.
qualify-compiler-release.py --verify-release runs for the published release of that commit.

On the refused paths: the script runs with the checks run at a descendant commit, with one required job with no conclusion, with the release tag at another commit, and with no passed release decision.
expected_result: The first run exits 0 and writes a qualification record that names the commit, the decision, the checks run and the signed artifact run. The verify run exits 0 and records the digest of every asset, equal to the qualified artifacts. Each refused run exits non-zero, names its cause, and writes no qualification record.
notes: The test runs the script as a process, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records; it reaches no GitHub service.

title: A passed release decision publishes the commit's release, which qualifies through the consumer path, and every refused path publishes nothing
steps: With a commit whose release decision passed and whose signed artifact run succeeded: the publish-release job runs.
The job verifies the decision, fetches the four assets by their artifact IDs, verifies them, and creates the release compiler-<commit>, not the latest, with the release output.
The qualify-release job runs with that output and qualifies the release through the consumer path.
On the refused paths: the job runs with a refused decision, with no decision, with an existing tag, and with an archive whose digest differs from the listed one.
expected_result: The main run publishes exactly the four assets, prints the release URL, and the qualification record names the passed decision, the release and the signing run. Each refused run fails, names its cause, and creates no release: the existing tag is named.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: Applying the plan writes the platform requirements with the rest of the generated files
steps: The service author runs the stego binary, apply, in the project folder of the test data set.
expected_result: It exits 0. The plan lists the platform requirements file with the other generated files, the file states the nine needs of the components, and the generation record lists the file with its hash.

title: Checking an environment file that supplies each need reports that it meets every requirement
steps: The operator runs the stego binary, env check, with --requirements and the environment file of the test data set.
expected_result: It exits 0, reports that the environment meets each requirement, names no unmet requirement and lists no unused value.

title: A push builds, checks and signs the image through the platform's pinned shared pipeline
steps: The service author pushes the service of the test data set to the test repository on the hosted CI provider.
The generated CI file calls the platform's shared pipeline at the pinned commit, which runs the STEGO checks, builds the application and the image, and signs it keyless.
expected_result: The run passes. Drift, vet, test, the reproducible build and the executable match each passed before the publish step. The published image's signature verifies against the identity of the shared pipeline at the pinned commit, and its executable digest equals the one in the build record of the run.

title: A new ci-pipeline version reaches each service as a change of one pin
steps: The platform engineer runs the stego binary, registry release, for ci-pipeline with a new shared pipeline commit, in the registry copy of the test data set.
The service author of each of two services that use the registry copy runs the stego binary, apply.
expected_result: Each apply exits 0, and git diff of each service shows one changed line in its CI file, the pin, and in the generation record only the new hash of the CI file, with no other change.

title: Argo CD deploys the service from STEGO's base and the platform's overlay
steps: The operator runs the stego binary, env check, on the environment file of the GitOps repository against the service's platform requirements, and it passes.
The operator commits the overlay to the GitOps repository.
Argo CD syncs the application that the ApplicationSet makes for the environment test.
expected_result: The application is synced and healthy. The Deployment in the namespace orders-test runs the image by the digest that the overlay sets, with two replicas and the PodDisruptionBudget of the overlay, and with the probes and default resources of the base.
notes: Runs in the jshell cluster test namespace only. The unmet path waits for ST-DLV-Q02.

title: Applying the plan writes the CI file for the provider the delivery stanza names
steps: The service author runs the stego binary, apply, in the project folder of the test data set, whose delivery stanza names the hosted CI provider.
expected_result: It exits 0. The plan lists the CI file, which calls the platform's shared pipeline at the pinned commit and the STEGO checks by pin, and the generation record lists it with its hash.

title: Applying the plan writes the Kubernetes base and then the ApplicationSet from the delivery stanza
steps: The service author runs the stego binary, apply, in the project folder of the test data set.
The run writes the Kubernetes base, and from the delivery stanza the ApplicationSet.
expected_result: It exits 0. The plan lists the base and the ApplicationSet; the base builds with plain kustomize; the ApplicationSet names the service, the project orders and the base, and its files generator lists the platform's environment files.

title: An agent scaffolds a fill, writes its rule and its test, binds it, and stego test records its evidence
steps: With a project from stego init --archetype rest-crud, the built-in registry and stego apply run once with no fill bound: stego fill create admin-policy --slot before_create --collection org-users runs, and go vet runs over fills/admin-policy.

The agent replaces the unfinished policy with a rule that denies a caller who is not an admin the creation of an admin, adds a test of that rule, binds admin-policy at before_create of org-users in service.yaml, and runs stego test.
On the misfit path: the binding names org-groups in place of org-users, and stego plan runs.
On the refused path: the agent removes the test file of admin-policy, and stego test runs; then the agent restores the test file, adds the import github.com/lib/pq, and stego test runs again.
expected_result: Expects fill create to exit 0 and to write fills/admin-policy/fill.yaml, code and a test file, and go vet of the scaffold to pass. Expects stego test to exit 0 and to write evidence into fill.yaml with the fill digest of admin-policy and the contract digest of before_create.proto. On the misfit path, expects plan to exit non-zero with a fault that admin-policy does not fit its binding, which names admin-policy, rest-api.before_create, the bound collection org-groups and the fill's collection org-users. On the refused path, expects each run of stego test to leave fill.yaml of admin-policy byte for byte as it was before the run, and to name why: no test file, then github.com/lib/pq.
notes: Not automated yet: stego test records no evidence, and no qualification check is built. The agent is a script, so the test is repeatable. Resolve github.com/lib/pq through a replace directive to a fixture module. admin-policy has no sign-off in this flow, so plan refuses it as unsigned too: the misfit path must find the fault of the fit, not any fault that names the fill. stego test runs go test over the fills, which needs the generated out/slots package; the first stego apply writes it.

title: The service author records evidence and signs it with a listed key, and the fill becomes qualified
steps: With untested-fill bound at before_create of org-users, and listed-ssh as the service author's signing key: the service author runs stego test.
The service author runs stego fill sign untested-fill, then stego fill status and stego plan.
On the failed path: the test of untested-fill-2 fails, and the service author runs stego test, then stego fill sign untested-fill-2.
On the unlisted path: the test of untested-fill-2 passes, the service author signs untested-fill-2 with unlisted-ssh, binds it at before_create of org-groups, and runs stego plan.
expected_result: Expects stego test to exit 0 and to write evidence for untested-fill; fill sign to exit 0 and to write a sign-off that ssh-keygen -Y verify accepts with the public key of listed-ssh; fill status to show untested-fill as qualified; and plan to exit 0. On the failed path, expects stego test to exit non-zero and to write no evidence for untested-fill-2, and fill sign to exit non-zero with a message that the fill has no evidence. On the unlisted path, expects plan to exit non-zero and to name untested-fill-2 and that SIGNERS does not list its key.
notes: Not automated yet: stego test records no evidence, and stego fill sign and stego fill status are not written.

title: An agent finds the fills for a slot with their standing, and each other path says what it found
steps: With the project of ST-EXT-TD01: the agent runs stego registry fills --slot before_create.
On the broken path: the fill.yaml of unsigned-fill is made invalid YAML, the agent runs the same command, the author repairs the file, and the agent runs it again.
On the empty path: the agent runs stego registry fills --slot after_delete.
On the refused path: the agent runs stego registry fills --slot befor_create.
expected_result: Expects the main run to exit 0 and to list each fill that implements before_create with its collection and standing, and not other-slot-fill. On the broken path, expects the first run to list unsigned-fill as unreadable with its fault, and the run after the repair to list it with the standing unsigned. On the empty path, expects exit 0 and output that names after_delete and stego fill create. On the refused path, expects exit non-zero and a list of the slot names that the active set declares.
notes: Not automated yet: runRegistryFills (ST-EXT-QRY01-H) shows no standing, and fill.CatalogReader is not written.

title: The service author finds a stale fill, records new evidence, signs it, and plan accepts the fill again
steps: With stale-fill bound at before_create of org-users, and listed-ssh as the service author's signing key: the service author runs stego fill status.
The service author runs stego test.
The service author runs stego fill sign stale-fill, then stego plan.
On the stopped path: before the new evidence, the service author runs stego plan and then stego apply.
expected_result: Expects fill status to name stale-fill as stale, with policy.go as the file that changed; stego test to exit 0 and to write new evidence; fill sign to exit 0 and to write a sign-off of the new evidence; and plan to exit 0. On the stopped path, expects plan and apply each to exit non-zero and to name stale-fill, and apply to write nothing to the out folder or the record.
notes: Not automated yet: stego fill status (ST-EXT-CH02) and fill.ListQualification (ST-EXT-QRY02-H) are not written. stego test records no evidence, and stego fill sign is not written.

title: An apply writes the code and its record together, and one commit holds both
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03: the service author adds a second entity to service.yaml and runs stego apply.
The service author commits the service folder with git add -A and git commit.

On the interrupted path: the author changes the declaration again, stego apply is stopped with SIGKILL after the journal is written, and stego plan, stego apply and stego drift run; then stego recover runs.
expected_result: stego apply exits 0 and writes the files of the new entity and a record that names every input digest and every file it wrote. The commit holds the record and every file it lists. On the interrupted path, plan, apply and drift each exit non-zero and name stego recover; after stego recover no journal remains, and the output matches the record.
notes: The interrupted path needs a test hook that stops apply at a named journal point, because a kill by timing does not reach each point. ST-GEN-INV01-T injects each point in the package. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: Drift names each generated file that no longer matches its hash, and a broken record is reported as broken
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03: the platform engineer runs stego drift on the unchanged service.
Two generated files under out are edited by hand, and stego drift runs again.
On the broken path: the files are restored, the registry content digest of the record is changed, and stego drift runs.
expected_result: The first run exits 0 and lists no drift. The second run exits non-zero and lists exactly the two edited files. The run on the broken path exits non-zero and says that the record is broken. No run changes a file.
notes: It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A component fix lands by a pin bump and one apply, and its diff holds the fix alone
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03 with the standing variant of ST-DIS-TD01: the service author moves the registry pin from R1 to R2.
The service author runs stego plan, which lists each file that the new digest of component A changes.
stego validate reports the standing of each pin, the successor included.
stego fill status reports that no fill is bound, so none needs qualification.
The service author runs stego apply.
The service author runs git diff and commits.
expected_result: Each run exits 0. The plan lists only files in component A's namespace and the record. After apply, git diff shows changes only in those files and in the record, where component A's digest is DA2 and the registry reference is R2. stego drift then exits 0.
notes: The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A declaration change regenerates the code, deletes what is no longer generated, and gives the same files twice
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03: the service author adds an entity Tag and removes the field title of Note in service.yaml.
stego validate reports the standing of each pin, and stego fill status reports that no fill is bound.
The service author runs stego apply, then stego apply again.
The service author runs git diff and commits the declaration, the code and the record.
On the failed path: a field of an unknown type is added, and stego apply runs.
expected_result: The first apply exits 0, writes the files of Tag, changes the files of Note, and deletes each file that the record lists and the new plan does not generate. The second apply exits 0 and changes nothing. The failed run exits non-zero, names the field, and changes no file.
notes: It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A saved plan lists every change, and apply then makes exactly those changes
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03: the service author adds an entity Tag and removes the field title of Note, and runs stego plan.
The service author reads the saved plan.
The service author runs stego apply with the saved plan.
On the stale path: the author plans again, edits service.yaml, and runs stego apply with that plan.
expected_result: stego plan exits 0, lists each file it would create, update or delete and that the record changes, and changes no file outside .stego. Apply writes exactly the files that the plan names. On the stale path apply exits non-zero, says that the plan is stale, and writes nothing.
notes: It waits on the saved plan: today stego plan saves nothing (ST-GEN-CLI03), and how apply is given a saved plan is not named yet. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: After an interrupted apply, drift names recover, and recover makes the files and the record agree
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03: the service author adds an entity Tag, and stego apply stops after the first operation of its journal.
The service author runs stego drift.
The service author runs stego recover.
On the conflict path: a second interrupted apply runs, a journaled file gets a third content, and stego recover runs.
expected_result: stego drift exits non-zero and names stego recover. stego recover exits 0, and then the output matches the new record and stego drift exits 0. On the conflict path stego recover exits non-zero, names the file, and changes nothing.
notes: It needs a test hook in the stego binary, enabled only in a test build, that stops apply at a named journal point, because a kill by timing does not reach each point. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A frontend build folder becomes one checked bundle, and a bad entry changes nothing
steps: The service author runs stego assets with --directory on a build folder of index.html and two assets, and --output bundle.zip.
The service author runs it again on the same folder.
On the refused path: a symbolic link is added to the folder, and stego assets runs with the same output.
expected_result: The first two runs exit 0 and write the same bytes. The refused run exits non-zero, names the link, and leaves bundle.zip as it was.
notes: It runs the stego binary in a temporary folder.

title: Apply writes the architecture view with the code, and a reader follows a request flow in it
steps: From ST-GEN-TD01: the service author runs stego apply.
The service owner opens the view in a headless browser with the network blocked, selects a component, and follows the request flow that creates a User.
On the refused path: a component of the active set loses its layer, and stego apply runs.
expected_result: Apply exits 0, and the record lists the view. The view opens with no network request, shows the four aspects, shows what the component connects to, and steps through the flow from the operation to the store and its events. The refused run exits non-zero, names the component and the missing layer, and writes nothing.
notes: The paths of the view and the model file are not named yet; the builder names them. It needs a real browser driven from Go in CI, not Playwright (AGENTS.md), and does not run on the developer workstation.

title: A change shows in the model diff, a stale view is drift, and an unchanged shape gives an empty diff
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03: the service author adds an entity Tag and runs stego apply, then git diff on the model file.
The author adds a YAML comment to service.yaml and runs stego apply.
On the refused path: the view is edited, and stego drift runs.
On the broken path: the record is cut off, and stego drift runs.
expected_result: The first diff shows the lines of Tag and no other change. The second apply leaves the model file byte-identical. Drift on the refused path exits non-zero and names the view. Drift on the broken path exits non-zero and names the record.
notes: The paths of the view and the model file are not named yet; the builder names them. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A service moves to the next declaration version by validate, fix, plan and apply
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03 with a registry that accepts only declaration version 3: the author runs stego validate on the declaration at version 2.
The author runs stego fix.
The author reads git diff, which shows service.yaml alone, and runs stego plan.
The author runs stego apply.
On the unfixable path: a construct that the rewrite cannot change is in the declaration, stego fix runs, the construct is rewritten by hand, and stego validate runs again.
expected_result: Validate exits non-zero and names the accepted version 3. Fix exits 0 and changes service.yaml only. Plan lists each generated file that changes. Apply exits 0, and the record states version 3. On the unfixable path fix names the construct with its path and writes nothing, and the last validate exits 0.
notes: The field of the declaration version and the registry's list of accepted versions are not named yet; the builder names them. The registry copy of ST-GEN-TD03 gets versions 2 and 3, with a rewrite from 2 to 3 that renames one key. It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.

title: A service moves its pin to the promoted component and regeneration changes no file
steps: From ST-GEN-TD03 with component A promoted from a team's local registry to the common registry with the same digest: the service author moves the service's pin to the common registry.
The service author runs stego apply and then git status.
expected_result: Apply exits 0, git status shows no change under out, and stego drift exits 0.
notes: It runs the stego binary that the test builds once per run from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network.
